facts.statement: Fossils of Palaeortyx date from the Middle Oligocene to the Early Pleistocene.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Oligocene to Early Pleistocene

facts.statement: The genus Palaeortyx was described by Milne-Edwards in 1869.
Six species are recognized within the genus Palaeortyx, including P. caluxyensis, P. edwardsi, P. gallica, P. intermedia, P. major, and P. miocaena.
facts.quote: subdivision: Palaeortyx caluxyensis Palaeortyx edwardsi Palaeortyx gallica Palaeortyx intermedia Palaeortyx major Palaeortyx miocaena

facts.statement: Palaeortyx was an extinct bird that ate seeds.
facts.quote: Palaeortyx is an extinct genus of granivorous galliform bird

facts.statement: Palaeortyx lived from the early Eocene to the early Pliocene.
facts.quote: It lived from the early Eocene to the early Pliocene

facts.statement: It is debated whether Palaeortyx belongs to the family Phasianidae or Odontophoridae.
facts.quote: It lived from the early Eocene to the early Pliocene, and may be a phasianid or odontophorid

facts.statement: Fossils of Palaeortyx have been found in Germany, France, Italy, Hungary, and Romania.
facts.quote: It is known from several fossils found in Germany, France, Italy, Hungary and Romania

facts.statement: The parent group of Palaeortyx is the family Phasianidae.
Palaeortyx is classified in the family Phasianidae.
The time range for Palaeortyx is from the Rupelian to the Piacenzian, spanning 33.9 to 2.58 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rupelian to Piacenzian (33.9 to 2.58 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 30 recorded fossil occurrences of Palaeortyx in the Paleobiology Database.
